verdicts.title: A categorical equivalence between affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras and some quiver Hecke algebras
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Inspired by the work of Rostam, we establish an explicit categorical equivalence between affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras and quiver Hecke algebras associated to disjoint copies of quivers of (affine) type $A,$ generalizing Rouquier's categorical equivalence theorem.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses a categorical equivalence between affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras and quiver Hecke algebras, focusing on representation-theoretic structures. It does not mention CNF formulas, AC0 circuit depth, or any complexity-theoretic notions, nor does it connect Hecke algebra element orders to computational complexity measures.

verdicts.title: Dirac cohomology for the degenerate affine Hecke Clifford algebra
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We define an analogue of the Dirac operator for the degenerate affine Hecke-Clifford algebra. A main result is to relate the central characters of the degenerate affine Hecke-Clifford algebra with the central characters of the Sergeev algebra via Dirac cohomology. The action of the Dirac operator on certain modules is also computed. Results in this paper could be viewed as a projective version of the Dirac cohomology of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses Dirac cohomology and central characters in the context of the degenerate affine Hecke-Clifford algebra and Sergeev algebra, but does not mention CNF formulas, AC0 circuit depth, or any polynomial relationship between algebraic structures and computational complexity measures. The focus is on representation-theoretic results, not computational complexity.

verdicts.title: Affine Hecke algebras and quiver Hecke algebras
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We give a presentation of localized affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of arbitrary type in terms of weights of the polynomial subalgebra and varied Demazure-BGG type operators.
